title: JPMorganChase's new community outlook survey reveals how Chicagoans view the local economy, housing, careers and their personal finances.

# JPMorganChase's new community outlook survey reveals how Chicagoans view the local economy, housing, careers and their personal finances.


Nearly half of Chicago residents say peace of mind, financial security are financial priorities heading into 2027


CHICAGO


---


November 23, 2026


JPMorganChase has released local findings from its first-ever Community Outlook survey of the Greater Chicago area, measuring how residents view their financial lives, their communities, and their aspirations. In Chicago, the survey found that almost half of residents (49%) cited peace of mind and financial security as their biggest financial goals — the top priority by a wide margin — offering a detailed portrait of how the community is navigating economic conditions, cost-of-living pressures, career decisions, and its evolving definition of the American Dream.


"Chicagoans are telling us clearly that financial security is what matters most to them right now, and they are taking concrete steps to protect it," said Maria Holmes, Co-Chair of JPMorganChase's Illinois Market Leadership Team. "Our commitment is to meet residents where they are — helping them build savings, pay down debt, and access the tools and guidance that turn that goal into reality."


## Views on the local economy & achieving Chicagoans’ financial dreams


Residents shared their top financial goals, their outlook on home ownership, and how broader economic conditions are shaping their personal finances. The survey also captured sentiment around buying versus renting and what the American Dream means:


- Chicagoans are feeling a gap between their personal finances and the local outlook:


On the broader outlook, 38% of Chicago residents feel positive about their own personal finances (very or somewhat positive), while only 25% feel positive about their local economy — a feeling gap between personal circumstances and the wider economic picture. When asked about the direction of the local economy, responses leaned toward caution, with 42% saying it is holding steady and 41% describing it as declining.


- Chicagoans


want to build resiliency and plan for the future:


49% of Chicago residents said peace of mind/financial security is one of their most important financial priorities, followed by building an emergency fund (28%) and retirement/long-term savings (27%).
- The cost of housing is unaffordable


: On housing affordability, 52% rated housing in their area as somewhat or very unaffordable, and 44% of renters said 40% or more of their monthly income goes toward rent.
- How Chicagoans define the American Dream


: For over half (51%) of Chicago residents, the American Dream is best defined as financial independence, and by being able to afford day-to-day expenses without stress, followed by owning a home (50%).
- Smaller fraud & scam reports than the total survey average, but the impact is still lasting


: 30% reported having been targeted by a scam call in the past year, and 24% by a scam online, as compared to the average of the 13 markets surveyed at 33% and 27%, respectively.


To help address the need for more financial resources, in June, 2026 JPMorganChase[announced](https://www.jpmorganchase.com/newsroom/press-releases/2026/american-dream-initiative-doubling-down-on-community-banking) a significant expansion of its community banking efforts to help more people build the knowledge and confidence to manage their money, expanding financial health education programming with the goal of reaching 5 million people. These efforts are part of the firm’s[American Dream Initiative](https://www.jpmorganchase.com/newsroom/press-releases/2026/american-dream-initiative-announcement) , a multi-year effort to help expand financial health education, equip customers with digital tools, strengthen fraud and scam prevention through education and protections and advance policy solutions to support young people’s financial futures.


"Chicago is a city of resilient, resourceful people, and this data reflects a community that is planning carefully and prioritizing stability," said Jared Evans, Community Manager, Chase. "We’re investing locally — in branches, in small business support, in financial health tools, and in fraud protection — to help residents pursue the security they told us matters most."


## Housing & cost of living changing spending habits


The survey also explored where residents are tightening their budgets, where spending has increased, and how they expect to spend during the upcoming holiday season.


- Chicagoans cut restaurant spending, more on dining in


: Over half (55.28%) have cut back on dining out, the most common category, followed by entertainment (42.45%). While 38% reported increased spending on groceries over the past year, the top category for rising costs.
- Tightening the wallet this holiday season:


Almost half 49% of Chicago residents plan to spend less on travel this holiday season compared to last year, and 46% plan to spend less on gifts.
- Finding value in both home ownership and renting


: 56% cited home ownership as important for financial stability, while 53% (strongly plus somewhat agree) said renting makes more financial sense than owning for some people, reflecting a community weighing both paths.
- As part of its American Dream Initiative, JPMorganChase is aiming to deploy $750 billion to help increase housing supply and support homeownership opportunities. The multi-year effort to expand economic opportunity also focuses on advancing small business growth, improving financial health, helping people secure good jobs, expanding access to quality healthcare and strengthening local institutions in Chicago and communities across the country.


## Views of the local job market are mixed


In the midst of a job market with moderate amount of opportunity, as described by over half (58) of Chicago residents, 33% said it is hard to get a job, Confidence in finding a new job locally is also guarded, with almost half (49%) feeling somewhat or very challenged about the prospect.


When it comes to starting their own business, only 18% of Chicagoans plan to start a business within the next two years, most often motivated by passion (33%), followed by achieving the “American Dream” (17%) and local customer demand (13%). While 75% agree that Chicago is a place where local businesses can thrive.


## Chicago residents choose local news over social media


The survey revealed how closely residents follow economic news, where they source information about their local economy, and whether that coverage has influenced major life decisions. Sixty-eight percent of Chicago residents said they follow local economic news very or somewhat closely. Sixty-one percent get their news from local TV news, the most common source, followed by social media platforms (45%).


Chicagoans also said news consumption impacted their wallets, with 32% said local news coverage of the economy prompted them to think about saving more, and 28% said it prompted them to actually save more money.


For more than 165 years, JPMorganChase has been working to advance an economy that works for all in Greater Chicago, by leveraging its expertise, insights, and resources to help residents, businesses, and communities achieve their goals. Across Greater Chicago, the firm serves nearly 4.4 million consumer customers, nearly 420,000 small business customers and has about 13,600 employees.


Since 2021, the firm has provided more than $105 million in philanthropic contributions to help strengthen local communities, increase opportunities, and drive long-term economic growth across Greater Chicago.


To learn more about the firm’s impact in Chicago, visit


[https://www.jpmorganchase.com/communities/chicago](https://www.jpmorganchase.com/communities/chicago)


## About the survey & methodology


The Community Outlook survey was conducted by Morning Consult on behalf of JPMorganChase, measuring how residents view their financial lives, their communities, and their aspirations. Interviews were conducted online between August 24 and September 11, 2026, among a total of 7,800 U.S. adults ages 18 and older, split evenly across 13 metropolitan areas: Boston, Washington, D.C., Miami, Philadelphia, Columbus, Atlanta, Chicago, Dallas/Fort Worth, Seattle, the San Francisco Bay Area, Los Angeles, and Birmingham. Figures for Chicago reflect responses from approximately 602 residents in the Chicago metropolitan area, including Chicago-Naperville-Elgin, IL-IN-WI. Results carry a margin of error of approximately ±4.0 percentage points at the 95% confidence level, and wider for subgroups. Because several cross-market differences fall within the margin of error, some readings are described as directional rather than definitive.
